articleTitle: Proposal of Radio High-way Networks for future multimedia-personal wireless communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Air interfaces of the mobile communication is widely spreading, because of the diversified service demands, technology trends and radio propagation conditions. This paper proposes the Radio High-way Networks that is universally applicable for any mobile services and any mobile radio air-interfaces. The system is constructed by using microcellular radio links and wide-band optical virtual free spaces, and the radio signal is guided by the virtual free space as radio signal format. As one pragmatic solution for the Radio High-way Networks, we select the PAM/IM/TDMA methods and give the routing algorithm, required sampling frequencies and the available capacity.

articleTitle: Advanced wireless access system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes an advanced wireless system which is composed of a wireless access node, a wireless access point, and a multimedia portable terminal. The wireless access node and access point are connected by optical fibers to realize broadband and high quality transmission. The radio frequency spectrum is directly carried on optical fibers using "fiber radio" technologies. This advanced wireless system, the multimedia wireless access system, provides video and data communications as well as voice services.

articleTitle: A new criterion for processing handover requests in mobile cellular networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: A new prioritization scheme based on dynamic priority queueing, for processing handover requests in mobile cellular networks is presented. The queues are periodically reordered depending on the radio power levels received by mobile subscribers from base stations and the rate of power degradation. The new scheme improves service quality of the cellular system by reducing handover failure probability as compared to the measurement-based prioritization scheme. Such improvements are demonstrated via simulated experiments.

articleTitle: Wireless telecommunications technologies for rural applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Wireless access technologies are becoming progressively less expensive than the various wired alternatives and offer the further advantages of rapid and flexible deployment in both urban as well as rural areas. In spite of the strong political incentives to improve telecommunications in rural areas the practical deployment of the various available technologies in developing countries is often difficult. There are several reasons for these deployment difficulties. (1) The start-up capital costs are high. (2) The equipment may be more suited to the needs of a developed country than to the telecommunication needs of a developing or newly industrialized country. (3) The tradeoff between labour and material costs in the system design have not been made for the economic realities of a developing country. (4) The equipment is not designed to integrate into the existing technology structure for the country of use. (5) Affordable equipment may soon become obsolete and hence difficult and expensive to maintain. (6) The three basic telecommunications services; voice, facsimile, and in-band data are not all readily available. (7) The rural service quality may not be equivalent to that of urban systems. (8) The available spectrum may be inadequate. We look at each of the above points to determine the impact on the required equipment.

articleTitle: Action COST 231: a commitment to the transition from GSM to UMTS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Current mobile communications market analyses indicate that Europe is mobile aware and entering the consumer market. Although incompatibility is the essential weakness between today's cellular, paging, cordless and mobile data services, their strength lies in their responsiveness to customer demand in a variety of different public and private market sectors with an element of service-creation flexibility and standardisation of the individual system-access technology. The progressive migration from second to third generation systems, expected to start at the turn of the century, must hence be undertaken while ensuring that the current user markets will perceive such a service evolution as relatively seamless, attractive and natural. In this process, the main goal of COST 231 Action is to provide a suitable support to the efforts of both standardization and research bodies, taking into account the technological developments foreseen in mobile and fixed telecommunication networks.

articleTitle: Comparison of multiple-accessing schemes for mobile communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper addresses the optimum choice of multiple accessing for the emerging mobile and personal communication systems. It highlights the critical characteristics of a mobile radio environment that play a key role in the choice of multiple access and then assesses the suitability of digital multiple access techniques namely, time division multiple access (TDMA) and code division multiple access (CDMA) to meet the growing needs of the mobile communication industry. The channel capacity of three multiple access schemes, viz. FDMA, TDMA and CDMA, is compared under the assumption of both forward and reverse link power control and the CDMA is shown to outperform the other two in the mobile radio environment.

articleTitle: Optimal design of error control schemes for packet radio networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of designing a "virtual error free channel" for communication over unreliable (cellular) packet radio channels using hybrid error control schemes. For hybrid error control to be effective it is essential that an optimal mix of forward error correction and automatic repeat requests be used. Further, the design of hybrid error control schemes depends critically on the application (for example, its traffic characteristics and quality of service it demands). We discuss data transfer and packet voice applications. Optimal design methodologies for performance metrics and applications of interest are developed. In addition, several numerical examples are presented.

articleTitle: Wireless technology evolution and impact on the access network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: "A wireless revolution is set to transform the world's telecommunications industry." Key to this discontinuity are three forces; unparalleled deregulation, privatization and competition in traditionally monopolistic local access telecommunications markets, the reallocation of hundreds of MHz of spectrum, and rampant technological progress in radio-based subscriber access systems. This paper reports on the third component, wireless technology as the involving transport mechanism for providing basic telephone service, particularly in developing countries.

articleTitle: Integration of wireless local area data communication to digital cordless telephone channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a wireless local area data communication system, which is integrated to digital cordless telephone systems: data signal is transmitted through digital cordless telephone channels, even if they are occupied by voice signals: the silence periods of voice communication are used for data transmission. A method is proposed to prevent voice communication from being interfered by the data transmission. A packet reservation technique is introduced to enhance the data transmission performance. Computer simulation results show the feasibility of the integrated voice and data wireless local area network.

articleTitle: A small domain communications system for personalized shopping assistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: By integrating wireless, video, speech and real-time data access technologies, a unique shopping assistant service can be created that personalizes the attention provided to a customer based on individual needs, without limiting his movement, or causing distractions for others in the shopping center. We have developed this idea into a service based on two products: a very high volume hand-held wireless communications device, the PSA (Personal Shopping Assistant), that the customer owns (or may be provided to a customer by the retailer), and a centralized server located in the shopping center to which the customer communicates using the PSA. The centralized server maintains the customer database, the store database and provides audio/visual responses to inquiries from tens of customers in real-time over a small area wireless network.

articleTitle: Radio in local loop for rural and sub-urban environments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper is focusing on various technologies for radio in the local loop (RLL). Special attention is paid to rural and sub-urban areas. Economical calculations are carried out for a digital cordless system (DECT) demonstrating the competitiveness of wireless solutions as compared to traditional copper wires. The calculations were done with the tools developed within RACE 2087/TITAN-project.

articleTitle: Development of CDMA cellular mobile communications system in Korea
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Korea has prepared for major structural changes to the country's mobile communications regime. The government recognized the CDMA technology as a national standard for the digital cellular system, and selected the second operator for running the digital cellular service, and what is more now the designation of FCS operators is under discussion. This paper introduces the CDMA based infrastructure which is being developed by ETRI jointly with domestic manufacturers in terms of the architecture, the design philosophy and the further progress.

articleTitle: Some good block PSK real number codes for Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: PSK real number codes for the Rayleigh fading channel were proposed by Jin and Periyalwar (see Sixth Annual International Conference on Wireless Communications, Calgary, Canada, July 1994). This paper tabulates the detailed mapping of some simple full-diversity low-delay codes in the original and the manually refined forms. The performance is examined by simulation at various interleaving depths. For the codes considered, the manually refined ones are found to be easy to implement and offer very little performance loss compared with the original.

articleTitle: Cost comparison of wireline and wireless access for the public switched telephone network (PSTN)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The access network has been considered to be the most costly part of the public switched telephone network. Traditionally, the subscriber lines have been based on copper wireline. Today, however, wireless technologies, e.g. cellular radio, can be used for this purpose as well. A cost comparison is made between the wireline and wireless access in order to find out the most feasible way to build new fixed subscriber lines. The comparison is based on a cost modelling study made by Nokia and Telecom Finland for the World Bank. The network alternatives were modeled on a study area which consisted of eight subareas each-having different characteristics. The investment costs covered the following equipment costs: exchange and the associated remote site equipment (concentrators, multiplexers and radio base stations), transmission equipment, infrastructure for equipment sites (including buildings, radio masts and antennas), and in-house cabling.

articleTitle: A fixed wireless cellular alternative to wireline telephony
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Modern business relies heavily on the information highway, i.e. the telecom network, to conduct day to day transactions. That highway consists of several interrelated systems, and networks, for example the wireline phone system and the cellular system to name two. Efficient mobile radio services are sought to be provided for a large number of customers by cellular systems. Mobile communication has gathered considerable importance and significance. The 'cellular' concept helps judicious use of the scarce frequency resource (by supporting frequency reuse and cell-splitting), while digital techniques enhance capacity and reduce system complexity. The present paper describes the feasibility and relevance of a telecommunication network which embeds concepts and features of the conventional wireline network and a cellular wireless network. The Hughes Network System Fixed Wireless GMH2000 System is used as an example to illustrate such an idea.

articleTitle: INSAT-mobile satellite communication services
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes the domestic mobile satellite communication system (MSCS) that is scheduled to be introduced in India in 1995/1996 as a part of the INSAT system. The INSAT MSCS will operate in the 2.6/2.5 GHz band. After briefly describing the need for a domestic MSCS, the reasons for selecting the S-band and the overall features of the system are given. The paper also describes the services, types of terminals, communication techniques, etc., that are to be introduced in the system and the communications capacity that would be available in the system.

articleTitle: Wireless trunked access through cellular radio and satellite systems for rural communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper describes some access methods for rural telecommunication using radio links as trunk lines. A comparison is made between different radio techniques including cellular radio and satellite. A design is described for a village network connected to the outside world through fixed cellular radio links. Some economical and technical aspects are analyzed.

articleTitle: Symbol synchronization for optical multi-pulse pulse position modulation systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The demand for high throughput and power efficient telecommunication systems can never be overstated. In this regard, optical multi-pulse pulse-position-modulation (MPPM) has received greater attention and has been proposed as an alternative to QPPM (4-ary PPM) for applications in high speed optical inter-satellite communications. Realizing the ever growing need for high capacity, our objective is to study symbol synchronization of optical MPPM, derive maximum likelihood synchronization rules, identify suboptimal rules that are easier to implement and evaluate their performance through computer simulations. We show that for high signal-to-noise ratios, perfect symbol synchronization can be achieved asymptotically in the limit of using long sequences of MPPM symbols.

articleTitle: DECT-based wireless local loop system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper describes a wireless local loop (WLL) system under development, based on the DECT air interface standard. The key features of DECT, in particular the use of dynamic channel selection, are described. Propagation measurements that indicate the typical spacing of base stations are reported. A WLL-PSTN interconnect architecture is proposed, and simulation results indicating its capacity are presented.

articleTitle: Wireless solution to rural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: We are in the midst of communication revolution and the last two decades have witnessed an explosion in new telecommunication technologies and services. This paper describes the features of the wireless radio network (WRN) and its applications in the Indian telecom network both in rural and secondary switching areas. The WRN system comprises of a mobile switching centre which houses the cellular controller unit, a radio base station and a wireless subscriber unit. The discussion touches upon the design, implementation, operation and maintenance aspects of the wireless radio network.

articleTitle: Estimation of location and hand-off indicators in radio communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: We describe a method for estimating deterministic components of signals in a colored noise background. This has applications in radio location or identification systems where deterministic tones are transmitted by a queried remote unit. The technique may also find use in radio communications systems where hand-off indicators such as received signal strength need to be measured in an unknown noise background.

articleTitle: Technology choices for PCN/PCS development in India
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The article reviews the status of competing technologies based on the DCS-1800, DECT and the CDMA. In India plans for a nation-wide cellular mobile telephony service (CMTS) based on GSM are underway while the CDMA are being proposed extensively for wireless loop applications. The Indian scene shall witness a high growth of wireless technologies whether for providing basic telephone service or other services such as PCS. The infrastructure being built now will have to favour a cost-effective and smooth migration to PCS.

articleTitle: Future public land mobile telecommunication systems for developing countries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper describes the general information about the activities being carried out in ITU-R on the future public land mobile telecommunication systems (FPLMTS) and its use in the developing countries for providing telecommunication services in an economical way so as to bridge the gap between the developed and the developing countries in the area of the telecommunications.

articleTitle: Spectrum considerations for satellite based personal communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The technological advances in mobile satellite systems (MSS) have brought the world to the threshold of realization of the ultimate in personal wireless communications-the hand-held satellite telephone-that could keep us in touch with each other, any time, any where, whenever needed. Inmarsat, the pioneering mobile satellite service organization providing services all across the globe, has been engaged in this evolutionary process of developing increasingly smaller mobile earth stations in keeping with the service demands. Satellite based personal communication services are basically an integral part of MSS and could be provided through non-geostationary satellite orbit mobile satellites in the service link spectrum allocated to MSS. Feederlinks to MSS satellites are generally accommodated in the spectrum allocated to FSS. The paper discusses various technical and regulatory aspects associated with the selection of frequency spectrum for a satellite based PCS system and identifies some possible solutions.

articleTitle: Capacity estimation of INSAT II transponders for VSAT operations in C and Ku bands
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Calculations of the capacity of the INSAT II transponders (C and Ku frequency bands) for VSATs designed for interactive data network applications are presented. A variety of multi-access protocols for different network performance objectives, and traffic delay parameters are taken into consideration. These typical capacities that can be achieved with C and Ku band transponders are equally applicable to other similar domestic satellite networks.

articleTitle: An optimised version of CCITT ADPCM and echo canceller for VSAT network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Tremendous interest is currently devoted to the development of VSAT (Very Small Aperture Terminal) network architectures providing voice communications in addition to data. In order to provide good voice communication, an efficient and cost effective voice interface becomes necessary. A DSP implementation often provides a desired solution of realising a low bit rate voice coder and an echo canceller effectively. This paper describes an effective implementation of CCITT G726 voice coder with optimisations (specific to the ISD-16/sup */ VSAT Network) and an echo canceller on a single DSP. Chip TMS320C25. The speech coder is an ADPCM coder and the echo canceller uses NLMS (normalised least mean squared algorithm with block update).

articleTitle: Wireless access networks and technologies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The growth in the deployment of wireless networks has been driven by the need for ubiquitous service and rapid deployment of telecommunications infrastructure. This paper describes several network topologies and architectures to illustrate wireless systems and their applications. A comparison is made of the radio access technologies available for these systems. A review of the key enabling technologies which support the introduction of these networks is provided.

articleTitle: Broadband-CDMA: one phone for a wireless twenty first century
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: We are in the midst of a revolution in telecommunications. Worldwide economic development coupled with the need for increased mobility has created a need for the immediate installation of a very large number of telephones. To meet this need and to accommodate the requirement of mobility, one must employ wireless telecommunications. Wireless systems are currently in wide, ever increasing, use in the US, UK, Europe, and all of Asia. Systems include fixed wireless local loop as well as cellular and PCS. In many areas of the world, second generation systems are being installed and third generation systems ordered. Multimedia and data services are being added to the basic voice service currently available. This paper discusses this evolution and explains why broadband-CDMA (B-CDMA) is required to meet the service and capacity needs of the 21st Century.

articleTitle: An architecture for deploying wireless services
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: We present an architecture to efficiently provide both voice and data services where the nature of the service or the data provided by the service may differ from one geographical region to another. The key to efficiency is to base the service at the local base station or switch.

articleTitle: Service integration in PCS using overlaid spread spectrum concept
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The upcoming personal communication services (PCS) require the need for integration of wireless services to provide for transmission of voice and data. The proposed system is simulated, (by considering Rayleigh faded channels) for two different data rates using the same spectrum and under moderate to high interference conditions. The integration concept using a decision feedback equalizer with a relatively short forward filter gives good performance and its usefulness in service integration is established.

articleTitle: Realizing the wireless future for universal personal communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Over the past five years, there has been rapid and sustained growth across the world in all segments of the wireless communications industry, particularly in cordless, cellular and paging. This growth has given rise to the view that wireless is permitting us to enter a new era in communications, characterized by a significant paradigm shift. The primary goal of universal telephone service is driving developing nations towards rapid provisioning of communications network infrastructure, often utilizing wireless technology as well as traditional wired means. Even as this is happening new developments and experience with wireless technology is helping us evolve towards the future state of universal personal communications (UPC), which promises the consumer the ability to communicate anywhere anytime and in any form i.e. voice, data, imaging and eventually full-motion video services. The paper examines the future of wireless communication.

articleTitle: Radio in the access network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Presently, there is an increasing interest in radio access as an alternative to other access technologies, because the existing radio technologies for fixed and mobile subscribers, might have advantages that make them superior to solutions based an wires for certain applications. To identify where the radio access presents potential advantages, it is necessary to identify the main parameters which define the applications, and then make a segmentation in terms of the most suitable technology to be used. This paper describes the parameters resulting from the performed analysis and a segmentation based an the Alcatel radio access solutions. Alcatel's portfolio is based on the following technologies: TDMA point to multipoint; fixed cellular terminals; DECT; and satellite communications. The paper concludes that the radio access environment is complex enough that general technology segmentations can be misleading. Only a detailed analysis in a case by case basis will determine the optimum solution.

articleTitle: Modified pragmatic code for land mobile satellite channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: A modified version of the pragmatic code has been designed for the laud-mobile satellite channel. It is done by the output symbol re-assignment approach. When evaluated using Monte Carlo simulation, this modified pragmatic code shows bit-error-rate improvement, typically in the region useful for digital speech applications.

articleTitle: Performance of trellis coded 8-PSK and 8-DPSK with convolutional interleaver in a fading mobile channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Error performance of trellis coded 8-PSK and 8-DPSK with and without interleavers has been investigated. Significant improvement in error performance is observed when convolutional interleaver is used. The insensitivity of a TCM scheme to the decoding decision depth is also observed for a fading channel.

articleTitle: Applications of wireless technology in the local loop in Hungary
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper briefly describes the situation of telecommunications in Hungary and gives an overview of the present and planned applications of wireless technology, while stresses the importance of some relevant regulatory questions, which can considerably affect the spread of radio access systems.

articleTitle: Public CT2 system with two-way calling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: In the current implementation of most CT2 systems, only handset initiated calls are allowed. The paper describes a design to allow two-way calling for the CT2 system with minimal modification to the current CT2 infrastructure as well as the public switched telephone network (PSTN). The design makes use of centralized databases in home location register (HLR) and visitor location register (VLR) to track the location of the handsets. A diagram of the CT2 two-way calling system is depicted. The authors also did a computer simulation of the proposed system to determine the potential area of congestion in the system.

articleTitle: Techno-economic considerations of wireless basic telephony in a wireline environment-the case of the developing nations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: With the emergence of a new era in information transfer heralded by the information highway, the telecommunications industry has begun looking at the access network as a possible framework for telephone service proliferation. While fibre connections remain as the preferred choice for the ultimate missing link, wireless telephone systems (WTS) are being considered to be an alternative to the copper-based access network. Because the wireless access network can be provisioned relatively quickly at a lower cost than the copper alternative, operators in both developed and developing countries have begun to evaluate WTS more seriously. This paper examines the opportunities that WTS provides for the developing nations as well as the technical and economic factors underlying its mass deployment in the basic services market. In the process, it addresses a variety of questions including (for example). Is the wireless solution a permanent one? Can it work with the existing wireline network? Does it provide a cost-effective solution? Is it upgradable to meet the needs of the diverse service demands? The resolution of these and other questions increasingly point towards the wireless access network as the way of the future for basic telephony in the developing nations.

articleTitle: A novel method to determine optimum cluster size for cellular radio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: A new and computationally efficient technique is presented for determining the optimum cluster size in presence of co-channel interference in a Rayleigh faded, lognormally shadowed mobile channel. The method is used to find the maximum traffic intensity per cell. Analytical results are included for typical cases with analog FM.

articleTitle: Techno-economic considerations for introduction of PCS in India
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Phenomenal progress in wireless technology and mobile radio networks in recent years has led to evolution of personal communication services (PCS) offering communication access to any one, any where, in any form. These developments provide India an opportunity to leapfrog from present state of far-from-satisfactory telecommunications to provision of a universal communication service. Major factors favouring introduction of PCS in India include : (i) enormous demand as yet unsatisfied for communications in rural, mobile and new industrial areas. (ii) adaptability for establishment of communication facilities in a quick timeframe (iii) flexibility to meet changing traffic pattern and provide modular growth. However, in India economic viability is an essential prerequisite for successful implementation of a PCS system. The telecommunication requirements in India are presented, and the techno-economic factors to be taken into consideration for the introduction of PCS are discussed.

articleTitle: DS/CDMA in indoor environments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The use of spread spectrum or code division multiple access (CDMA) has long been debated. This paper shows that the employment of techniques such as antenna diversity or fast power control schemes in indoor environments results in an significant increase in the capacity supported by the system, in addition to other advantages derived by the use of such techniques. The bandwidth efficiency is the parameter of quality used for systems comparison.

articleTitle: A regional satellite system for mobile communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Use of satellite systems in non-geostationary orbits for mobile communications is of wide interest. The paper presents a satellite system to meet the mobile voice and data (up to 4.8 kbps) communications requirements for users equipped with hand-held terminals in rural and unshadowed areas of the limited region of the globe bounded by 40/spl deg/N and 40/spl deg/S latitudes. After analysing the effect of parameters which have dominant effect on the definition of the space segment the paper establishes that by restricting the coverage requirements to this limited region the overall system would be much simpler to implement and manage. Finally the paper brings out how in comparison to other systems this scheme meets the system objectives most optimally with regard to both cost and complexity.

articleTitle: Impact of metered channel services on personal wireless communications in India
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: With the introduction of satellite communications in general and VSAT technology in particular in India, a whole new world of personal communications can be opened up, bringing with it new possibilities of business communications-data, voice or fax. This paper discusses in detail one such VSAT based product-the metered channel service and its impact on personal communication.

articleTitle: Sector-antenna diversity reception for a multipath fading channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: Personal wireless communication channels are characterized as multipath fading channels, where multipath delay spread is known to be a key parameter degrading the performance of a wireless communication system. In this paper, our previous works are reviewed to demonstrate that sector antenna diversity is a powerful means to mitigate the effect of multipath propagation. First, a convenient multipath delay spread estimation method is introduced. Then the usefulness of sector-antenna to reduce multipath delay spread as well as fading is discussed. This sector antenna diversity is then combined with a Viterbi equalizer, and its performance curve is shown.

articleTitle: Maximum-likelihood sequence estimation from subbands
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: In a paper by Rao and Pearlman (see Proc. IEEE-SP International Symposium on Time-Frequency and Time-Scale Analysis, p.69-73, Victoria, Canada, 1992), it has been shown that subband decomposition results in a reduction of memory in the subbands. Subband Decomposition is a technique in which the source spectrum is bandpass filtered and subsampled to obtain a time-frequency decomposition. Furthermore, the total prediction error power from the subbands is less than the fullband prediction error, for finite orders of prediction. In this paper we apply these results to equalizer design using subbands. It is shown that maximum-Likelihood (ML) sequence estimation in the subbands offers a gain in terms of estimation error. In addition, there is a considerable reduction in the computational complexity. It is also demonstrated that by working in the subband domain, it is possible to avoid the problems associated with the presence of nulls in the channel frequency response.

articleTitle: Personal communications services: challenges in technology integration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: The technological success of personal communication services (PCS) depends on advances in several disciplines: signal processing, communication and networking. Technical advances in these individual disciplines need to be accompanied by joint designs, and by clever integrations of component technologies on economical platforms for digital signal processing and computing, with user interfaces that are both friendly and compelling. Current examples of PCS are rudimentary but important initial steps in a field where the demand for additional functionality is rapidly increasing.

articleTitle: A connection management scheme for a mobile radio LAN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a novel connection management strategy for handling mobility in a radio LAN environment. The scheme provides a set of signalling operations for setting up and maintenance of the connections, involving the mobile entities in the network. For each roaming entity, a software agent, known as mobile representative, is used for insulating the users from the effects of mobility. Using these representatives and a novel connection caching strategy, foul-latency and scalable handovers are designed. Some experimental results, highlighting the performance of a prototype system, are included in the paper in order to indicate the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a programmable bit-rate multipulse excited LPC vocoder for digital cellular radio applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
abstract: We present the algorithm for design of an analysis-by-synthesis based multi-pulse excited/long-term prediction type LPC speech coder and discuss its real-time implementation using the state-of-art ADSP 2101 digital signal processor. The important features of this speech coder are attributed to the use of (i) an efficient search algorithm for computing the pulse locations and amplitudes involved, (ii) sigma-delta based 16-bit codec-filter VLSI chip: AD 28msp 0.2 acting as front and back ends (iii) perceptual weighting filter and (iv) an efficient output post-processing filter. A detailed objective and subjective evaluation of the speech coder is carried out.

publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 International Conference on Personal Wireless Communications
